This guide is for researchers who start a register-based study on the
Statistics Denmark (DST) research servers and do the data work themselves in R.
It is written with clinicians and PhD students in mind. You do not need
experience with registers, and the R you need to begin with is in phase 2.

It assumes that your project already has access to DST and that your registers
have been delivered. It does not cover how to apply for data, and it does not
teach statistical methods: the analysis pages show which R tools fit a register
study and point to courses and books for the theory.

The guide is organised as 14 numbered phases, from planning a study to
getting the results out through DST's output control. If you are new, start at
[phase 1 - Plan your study](plan-your-study.qmd) and take the phases in order;
the links at the bottom of each page lead to the next one. If you already know
R and only need the DST side, start at [phase 3 - Log in to
DST](log-in-dst.qmd). The look-up pages further down are for use as you go.

To find something, use the search box in the top bar for exact words, or
[Search by meaning](search.qmd) when you do not know what the guide calls it or
want to search in Danish.

## The phases of the guide

What each phase covers. The sidebar groups the phases into five stages.

  | Phase                                                              | Contents                                                                        |
  | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | [1 - Plan your study](plan-your-study.qmd)                      | Research question, key concepts and data model                                  |
  | [2 - R: the bare essentials](r-intro.qmd)                       | The minimum of R you need to get going                                          |
  | [3 - Log in to DST](log-in-dst.qmd)                             | From the first login to a running RStudio                                       |
  | [4 - File types and loading](file-formats.qmd)                  | Which file type opens with what, and lazy vs full loading                       |
  | [5 - Extracting data step by step](extraction-step-by-step.qmd) | The extraction pattern used throughout: open, filter, select, collect |
  | [6 - First extraction](first-extraction.qmd)                    | A complete extraction to a saved dataset, run on synthetic data on your own computer |
  | [7 - Inspect your data](inspect-data.qmd)                       | Check structure, types and distributions before analysis                        |
  | [7b - Check your delivery](delivery-check.qmd)                  | Six checks of the registers your project was actually given                     |
  | [8 - Find your registers](find-your-registers.qmd)              | Find the right registers for exposure, outcome and covariates                   |
  | [9 - Hospital contacts (LPR)](understand-lpr.qmd)               | How LPR2 and LPR3 are built, ICD codes, and extracting diagnoses                |
  | [10 - Build your study population](build-study-population.qmd)  | Cohort, index date, in/exclusion; comparison cohort, case-control, other designs |
  | [11 - Extract variables](extract-variables.qmd)                 | Outcomes, socioeconomics, comorbidity, medication and lab results for the cohort |
  | [12 - Assemble and prepare the dataset](data-manipulation.qmd)  | Joins, long and wide format, missing data and time-varying variables            |
  | [13 - Analysis](analysis.qmd)                                   | Choosing a method, Table 1, figures, regression, survival, rates, weighting      |
  | [14 - Export and repatriation](export.qmd)                      | Get your results safely out of DST                                              |

  | [Overview of registers](register-reference.qmd)        | look up column names, types and join keys for the most used registers (check them against your delivery) |
  | [Find a variable](find-a-variable.qmd)                 | look up which register a given variable lives in                                                   |
  | [Format tables](formatting-tables.qmd)                 | translate codes to text (municipality, education and employment codes) with DST's SAS format files |
  | [Parquet and fastreg](parquet-and-fastreg.qmd)         | point fastreg at your registers, or convert SAS files to parquet                                   |

  | [Good coding practice](good-coding-practice.qmd)       | write code you can still trust in six months: structure, naming, reproducibility                   |
  | [DST pitfalls](dst-pitfalls.qmd)                       | check the traps where your code runs and the answer is quietly wrong                               |
  | [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd)                 | work out a red error message, or an empty result, and find where to ask                            |
  | [Algorithms & special packages](packages-overview.qmd) | use a ready-made algorithm, such as the OSDC diabetes classifier or the Nordic Multimorbidity Index (NMI) |

## Want to help?

If you have reusable code for register work, for example weighted medication
use, family linkage or building episodes, drafts are welcome. [Want to
help?](contribute.qmd) says what is most useful and how to send it.
